questions.prompt: A CI job creates a namespace per pull request and deletes nothing. After a quarter, what is the most likely state of the cluster?
choices: Fine: Kubernetes garbage-collects namespaces nobody has used for 30 days
Fine: namespaces without running pods cost nothing
Each namespace is deleted automatically when the branch is deleted in Git
Dozens of namespaces for merged or abandoned pull requests, still running pods that hold requested CPU and memory, plus volumes and other leftovers
questions.explanation: Kubernetes has no notion of a namespace's lifetime and knows nothing about Git. Unless something deletes them, preview namespaces and everything they request live forever, and the scheduler keeps reserving capacity for them.

questions.prompt: A namespace has a ResourceQuota with `requests.cpu: 1` and no LimitRange. A developer applies a Deployment whose container sets no resources. What happens?
choices: The pods run with no CPU request, because the quota only counts what is declared
The Deployment is created, but its ReplicaSet cannot create pods: quota admission refuses each pod with `must specify requests.cpu`, visible in the ReplicaSet's events
`kubectl apply` of the Deployment fails with `exceeded quota`
The quota assigns each pod an equal share of the 1 CPU
questions.explanation: Quota is checked when pods are created, not Deployments. A quota on a compute resource requires every container to state it; without a LimitRange to fill in defaults, the ReplicaSet controller's pod creates are refused and the Deployment sits at 0 ready. `kubectl describe rs` shows the FailedCreate events.

questions.prompt: minienv's second reconcile reports 0 writes even though every live object has fields minienv never set (a Service's `clusterIP`, `imagePullPolicy`, quota `1Gi` where minienv wrote `1024Mi`). Why?
choices: `covers()` checks only that every field minienv wants is present in the live object, and compares quantities by value
Server-side apply rejects unchanged objects with 409
minienv caches the objects it wrote and never reads the cluster again
The API server strips its own defaults before returning objects
questions.explanation: Comparing a desired object with a live one for equality would always find differences, because the API server adds defaults and canonicalises quantities. A subset test with quantity-aware comparison makes 'unchanged' mean unchanged, so a settled cluster costs no writes and resourceVersions stay put.

questions.prompt: The GitHub API call that lists open pull requests fails with an expired token and the client returns an empty list. What should the reaper do?
choices: Delete every preview environment, since no pull request is open
Delete nothing and exit 0 silently
Still delete expired environments (the expiry is in the cluster), skip the closed-PR rule and warn, unless an operator passes --allow-empty
Delete the oldest half of the environments as a compromise
questions.explanation: An empty list is indistinguishable from an outage. Rules that depend only on data in the cluster (the expiry label) are still safe; the rule that depends on the external list must not act on input that looks like a failure. Better still, the fetch should raise on an error instead of returning an empty list.

questions.prompt: After a preview namespace is deleted, the storage bill keeps growing. What is the most likely leftover, and how does minienv's reaper find it?
choices: Pods stuck in Terminating; it lists pods in all namespaces

PersistentVolumes with reclaim policy Retain, now Released, whose `spec.claimRef.namespace` still names the deleted namespace; it matches them by claimRef and deletes them before (or, as orphans, after) the namespace
ConfigMaps; it deletes them by name prefix
Container images on the nodes; it runs `crictl rmi`
questions.explanation: PersistentVolumes are cluster-scoped. Deleting the namespace deletes the claims, and a Retain volume stays Released with its claimRef intact. Nothing else will ever delete it, so the reaper must look outside the namespace.

questions.prompt: A team's preview app installs a CRD and a validating webhook as part of its chart. Which isolation unit fits?
choices: A namespace with a stricter ResourceQuota
A namespace with a default-deny NetworkPolicy
Any of them; CRDs are namespaced
A virtual cluster (or a real cluster): CRDs and webhooks are cluster-scoped, so in a shared cluster one preview's versions would affect every other preview and the platform itself
questions.explanation: Namespaces only isolate namespaced objects. A CRD or a webhook installed by one preview applies cluster-wide. A virtual cluster gives each preview its own API server, so cluster-scoped objects stay inside it, at the cost of an extra control plane per preview.
